subject: physics
pattern: Alternating Current gives about 8 to 10 marks: 1-mark and 2-mark questions on rms values, reactance, Q-factor and transformer, a 3-mark derivation (current through pure L or C, power in an LCR circuit) or numerical on a series LCR circuit, and a 5-mark derivation of impedance of a series LCR circuit or resonance. Examiners expect phasor reasoning, the phase relation between V and I, and final formulas with units.

questions.q: Define the root mean square (rms) value of an alternating current.
questions.answer: The rms value of an alternating current is that value of steady direct current which produces the same heating effect in a resistor in a given time as the alternating current does: $I_{rms} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt2} = 0.707\,I_0$.

questions.q: What is wattless current? Give the condition for it.
questions.answer: The current in an AC circuit that does no net work (zero average power) is called wattless current. It occurs when the phase difference between voltage and current is $90^\circ$, i.e. in a purely inductive or purely capacitive circuit, where power factor $\cos\phi = 0$.

questions.q: Write the expression for the resonant frequency of a series LCR circuit.
questions.answer: At resonance $X_L = X_C$, so $\omega_0L = \frac{1}{\omega_0C}$, giving $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$, i.e. $\nu_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$.

questions.q: The rms value of the domestic AC supply is 220 V. Calculate the peak value of the voltage.
Define the quality factor (Q-factor) of a series resonant circuit. Write its expression.
questions.answer: The Q-factor is the ratio of the voltage across the inductor (or capacitor) at resonance to the applied voltage; it measures the sharpness of resonance: $Q = \frac{\omega_0L}{R} = \frac{1}{\omega_0CR} = \frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}$. A larger Q means a sharper resonance curve and smaller bandwidth, $Q = \frac{\omega_0}{2\Delta\omega}$.

questions.q: Write the working principle of a transformer. Mention any two energy losses in a transformer.
questions.answer: A transformer works on the principle of mutual induction: a changing current in the primary coil produces a changing flux in the core, which induces an emf in the secondary coil. $\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}$. Energy losses: (i) copper loss (I$^2$R heating in windings), (ii) iron loss due to eddy currents, (iii) hysteresis loss, (iv) flux leakage. (Any two.)

questions.q: Define impedance of a series LCR circuit and write its expression.
questions.answer: Impedance is the total opposition offered by an LCR circuit to the flow of alternating current, equal to the ratio of the peak (or rms) voltage to the peak (or rms) current: $Z = \frac{V}{I}$. $Z = \sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}$ with $X_L = \omega L$ and $X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C}$. SI unit: ohm.

questions.q: Show that the current leads the applied voltage by $\pi/2$ in a purely capacitive AC circuit. Define capacitive reactance.
questions.answer: Let $v = V_0\sin\omega t$ be applied across a capacitor C. The charge $q = Cv = CV_0\sin\omega t$. Current $i = \frac{dq}{dt} = \omega CV_0\cos\omega t = \omega CV_0\sin\left(\omega t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$. So $i = I_0\sin\left(\omega t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ with $I_0 = \frac{V_0}{1/\omega C}$. Hence current leads voltage by $\frac{\pi}{2}$. Capacitive reactance $X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{2\pi\nu C}$ is the opposition offered by the capacitor to AC; unit ohm. It is infinite for dc and decreases with frequency.

questions.q: Show that the current lags behind the applied voltage by $\pi/2$ in a purely inductive AC circuit. Define inductive reactance.
questions.answer: Let $v = V_0\sin\omega t$ be applied across an inductor L of negligible resistance. The induced emf is $-L\frac{di}{dt}$, so $v = L\frac{di}{dt}$, i.e. $\frac{di}{dt} = \frac{V_0}{L}\sin\omega t$. Integrating, $i = -\frac{V_0}{\omega L}\cos\omega t = \frac{V_0}{\omega L}\sin\left(\omega t-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$. So $i = I_0\sin\left(\omega t-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ with $I_0 = \frac{V_0}{\omega L}$. Current lags voltage by $\frac{\pi}{2}$. Inductive reactance $X_L = \omega L = 2\pi\nu L$ is the opposition of the inductor to AC; unit ohm. It is zero for dc and increases with frequency.

questions.q: Derive an expression for the average power in an AC circuit. Hence define the power factor.
questions.answer: Let $v = V_0\sin\omega t$ and $i = I_0\sin(\omega t+\phi)$. Instantaneous power $p = vi = V_0I_0\sin\omega t\sin(\omega t+\phi) = \frac{V_0I_0}{2}\left[\cos\phi-\cos(2\omega t+\phi)\right]$. Over a full cycle the average of $\cos(2\omega t+\phi)$ is zero, so average power $P = \frac{V_0I_0}{2}\cos\phi = V_{rms}I_{rms}\cos\phi$. The factor $\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z}$ is the power factor. It is 1 for a pure resistor and 0 for a pure inductor or capacitor.
keywords: average of cos(2 omega t + phi) zero

questions.q: A series circuit has $R = 30\,\Omega$, $X_L = 50\,\Omega$ and $X_C = 10\,\Omega$ connected to a 100 V rms AC source. Find the impedance, the rms current, the power factor and the average power dissipated.
questions.answer: $Z = \sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2} = \sqrt{30^2+40^2} = 50\,\Omega$. $I_{rms} = \frac{V}{Z} = \frac{100}{50} = 2$ A. Power factor $\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{30}{50} = 0.6$. Average power $P = VI\cos\phi = 100\times2\times0.6 = 120$ W (also $I^2R = 4\times30 = 120$ W).

questions.q: Explain the construction and working of a transformer. Write the expressions relating voltages, currents and number of turns for an ideal transformer.
questions.answer: Construction: two coils, primary (N$_p$ turns) and secondary (N$_s$ turns), wound on a laminated soft-iron core. Working: an alternating voltage applied to the primary produces an alternating flux in the core, which links the secondary and induces an emf in it by mutual induction (the same flux per turn links both coils). For an ideal transformer $\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}$, and since input power equals output power, $V_pI_p = V_sI_s$, so $\frac{I_p}{I_s} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}$. Step-up transformer: $N_s>N_p$ (voltage increases, current decreases); step-down: $N_s<N_p$. Efficiency $= \frac{V_sI_s}{V_pI_p}\times100\%$.

questions.q: Using the phasor diagram, derive an expression for the impedance and the current of a series LCR circuit connected to an AC source $v = V_0\sin\omega t$.
questions.answer: Let the current be $i = I_0\sin\omega t$ (the same in R, L and C). Voltages: $V_R = I_0R$ (in phase with current), $V_L = I_0X_L$ (leads current by $\pi/2$), $V_C = I_0X_C$ (lags current by $\pi/2$). On the phasor diagram $V_L$ and $V_C$ are opposite, so their resultant is $(V_L-V_C)$, perpendicular to $V_R$. By Pythagoras the applied voltage amplitude $V_0 = \sqrt{V_R^2+(V_L-V_C)^2} = I_0\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}$. Hence the impedance $Z = \frac{V_0}{I_0} = \sqrt{R^2+\left(\omega L-\frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2}$ and the peak current $I_0 = \frac{V_0}{Z}$. The phase angle between voltage and current is $\tan\phi = \frac{X_L-X_C}{R}$: if $X_L>X_C$ the current lags the voltage, if $X_C>X_L$ it leads. Thus $i = I_0\sin(\omega t-\phi)$.

questions.q: What is resonance in a series LCR circuit? Obtain the expression for the resonant frequency and mention the characteristics of the circuit at resonance.
questions.answer: Resonance is the condition in which the current amplitude in a series LCR circuit is maximum because the inductive and capacitive reactances become equal. Current amplitude $I_0 = \frac{V_0}{\sqrt{R^2+(\omega L-1/\omega C)^2}}$ is maximum when $\omega L = \frac{1}{\omega C}$. Hence the resonant angular frequency $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$ and $\nu_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$. Characteristics at resonance: (i) $X_L = X_C$, so impedance is minimum, $Z = R$; (ii) current is maximum, $I_0 = \frac{V_0}{R}$; (iii) current and voltage are in phase ($\phi = 0$) and the power factor is 1; (iv) the voltages across L and C are equal and opposite and may exceed the source voltage by a factor Q. The circuit is called an acceptor circuit, used for tuning a radio receiver. Sharpness of resonance is measured by $Q = \frac{\omega_0L}{R}$.
